CONTEXT
• Situating information disorder in Asia and Pacific in its historical and
global context
- Information disorder a problem "going back to the ancients"
(Dalton 202l)
- Information disorder cannot be reduced to "good vs evil narrative"
(Ong 202l)
- Why information disorder continues to warrant our attention
• Long history of information disorder in Asia and Pacific Region
- Colonial- and post-colonial powers have manipulated information
for decades
- Current information disorder rooted in historical experience

- Decline in political participation
- Low voter turnout
- Corroding democracies
• Information disorder: Cause or consequence of democratic decline?

- COMPARATIVE PERSPECTIVE

INFORMATION DISORDER IN COMPARATIVE
PERSPECTIVE
Actors
• Mostly domestic actors, except in Kyrgyz Republic
• Government-led information most consolidated and consisted in Thailand
• Non-state actors play prominent role in all four case studies
• Information disorder reflection of broader power constellations
Narratives
• Rarely explicitly pro-authoritarianism or anti-democratic
• Main goal is to sow confusion and broaden existing societal rifts
• Narratives are highly context specific building on local anxieties and fears
11/15/21|

11/15/21|
INFORMATION DISORDER IN COMPARATIVE
PERSPECTIVE (cont.)
Causes
• Political and financial objectives.
• Creating and sharing distorted information as a social lubricant/ signaling
• Great appetite for alternative news sources after decades of state control
Tools
• Considerable variance in ways distorted information spreads
• Information disorder *not* an online phenomenon in any of the cases
Consequences
• Information disorder amplifies societal rifts but also depends on them
• Information disorder does not automatically lead to authoritarianism
